tagline: The river road keeps traces of its older course.
intro: West from Shasta near Redding, Highway 299 passes Whiskeytown Lake before reaching the Trinity River country. Beyond Weaverville it follows the river through Junction City and the smaller settlements toward Willow Creek, then continues toward Blue Lake near Arcata.

The road has moved more than once to ease the mountain grades and make room for a reservoir. Old stretches remain beside the highway, with abandoned bridges visible from the newer line, including an arch from 1923. Some crossings have outlived the roads that needed them.

moments.title: Whiskeytown
moments.text: The federal government refused the Whiskeytown name for the post office until 1952; ten years later the new lake began covering the town, and only some buildings were moved to higher ground.

moments.title: Junction City
moments.text: At Junction City the Trinity turns northwest, past a settlement first called Milltown for the mills that worked here.

moments.title: Willow Creek
moments.text: Where Highways 299 and 96 meet, Willow Creek gives the Bigfoot stories a home in a museum devoted to the creature.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Trinity Scenic Byway
